notes.4: Most candidates recognised that weight is measured in newtons.
notes.5: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly, with most candidates either forgetting to convert the grams into kilograms or dividing the 100g by g before multiplying by the acceleration due to gravity on Mars.
notes.7: Candidates showed a good understanding of equilibrium and most correctly identified the one block in equilibrium.
notes.9: Some candidates found this question challenging and showed little understanding of the method of determining the centre of mass of a lamina.
notes.11: Some candidates confused work done with power and others thought that useful work is done when an object is held stationary above the ground
notes.13: The majority of candidates incorrectly thought that the width of the tube would alter the height of the liquid column and showed little understanding of this method of measuring pressure.
notes.16: Candidates showed a good knowledge of the relative expansions of solids, liquids and gases.
notes.17: Many candidates were not aware that there is no change in the average speed of the particles as a gas condenses to form a liquid. The only change is a reduction in their potential energy as their separation decreases.
notes.19: Candidates showed a good understanding of energy transfer by conduction.
notes.21: Stronger candidates answered correctly. However, many candidates correctly identified the change of direction of propagation of the waves, but incorrectly thought that the wavelength (and hence the speed) of the waves would decrease on entering the deep water.
notes.22: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly, with many candidates thinking that the ray of light would make an angle of 45° with the table.
notes.24: Candidates showed a good knowledge of the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum that are used for specific jobs.
notes.25: Few candidates knew the basic fact that sound is transmitted by longitudinal waves and many were unaware that an echo is a reflection of a sound wave.
notes.26: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly.
notes.28: This question was answered well and candidates showed a good understanding of the mutual forces between charged objects.
notes.29: Most candidates were either unaware of what e.m.f. stands for or did not read the responses with sufficient care.
notes.33: Many candidates ignored the presence of the 4Ω resistor, only using the value of the 2Ω when calculating the current in the circuit.
notes.34: Many candidates did not recognise that the role of either a circuit-breaker or a fuse is to disconnect the live wire from the appliance and so did not select the correct answer.
notes.35: There was little understanding of the concepts of the motor effect. The spread of the responses indicated that there was widespread guessing.
notes.38: Another question where detailed and careful reading was requires. The question referred to the nucleus of carbon, not the atom itself. Many candidates chose the response which described the complete atom.
notes.key_messages: Candidates should be reminded to read the questions carefully to ensure they understand what is being
notes.general_comments:
Candidates answered questions 2, 4, 7, 16, 19, and 28 well but found questions 5, 9, 11, 13, 17, 21, 22, 25,
26, 29, 33, 34, 35 and 40 more challenging.
